reason: B is the stronger proposal because reducing stand-off distance directly targets deposition efficiency, porosity, and in-flight oxidation while retaining the specified 15–45 μm feedstock, and it provides a controlled, falsifiable comparison. Although it largely extends an already reported spray-distance trend and overstates the likelihood of more complete melting at shorter residence time, A is less physically reliable because larger particles may remain insufficiently molten under unchanged spray parameters and its cited evidence does not support the predicted thickness gain.
